generated_output.summary: The Read tool's line_offset parameter fails when using third-party OpenAI-compatible models (like Qwen3.8-Flash) because these models serialize scalar integer arguments as JSON strings (e.g., "line_offset": "200"). The validation layer uses Ajv with type coercion disabled and a complex anyOf schema, resulting in an 'Invalid args' error and preventing tool execution.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: Third-party LLM providers serialize integer parameters into string representations in their tool call arguments (e.g., "line_offset": "200"). When validated against the tool schema using Ajv without type coercion enabled, strict type checking rejects the string values because they do not strictly match the expected integer/number type in the anyOf union.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect Ajv Validation Configuration
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect the Ajv validation setup in apps/kimi-code/src/main.ts to locate where tool argument validation and schema definitions (specifically for line_offset and anyOf unions) are initialized.

step_by_step_plan.title: Enable Type Coercion in Ajv Instance
step_by_step_plan.description: Update the Ajv validator instantiation in apps/kimi-code/src/main.ts to enable type coercion (setting { coerceTypes: true } or configuring appropriate options) so that string-serialized integer parameters like line_offset (e.g. "200") are properly coerced to numbers before schema validation.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add Regression Test for String-Serialized Numeric Arguments
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a unit/integration test case verifying that the Read tool successfully processes tool call arguments where numeric parameters like line_offset are passed as strings (e.g., {"line_offset": "200"}) without throwing an 'Invalid args' error.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run Test Suite
step_by_step_plan.description: Execute the verified test command to verify that all tests pass successfully and the regression is fully resolved.

structured_concepts.concept_name: JSON Schema Type Coercion in Ajv
structured_concepts.short_explanation: Type coercion allows a validation library to automatically convert input types (like a string containing a number "200") into the expected target type (like the integer 200) before validation.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Different LLM providers serialize JSON tool call arguments differently; enabling type coercion ensures that minor serialization differences do not break tool execution.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Enabling coercion or handling string-wrapped numbers in the validator prevents third-party model outputs from failing strict schema validation.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: An anyOf schema validation rule requires that the provided data matches at least one of the specified sub-schemas.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Complex union schemas can make validation stricter and harder for external models to satisfy if type matching is rigid.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The line_offset parameter uses a compound anyOf integer schema which exacerbates strict type rejection when values arrive as strings.

common_pitfalls: Disabling strict validation for unknown properties while attempting to fix type coercion.
Modifying prompt instructions instead of fixing the underlying schema validation layer.
